evals.prompt: Audit dotfiles/agents/.agents/skills/simplify/SKILL.md for improvements across models. Suggest changes only. Do not edit the file. Preserve its changed-diff scope and safety checks.
evals.expected_output: Give specific suggestions based on evidence. If no edit is justified, state that finding. Do not recommend blanket deletion of reasoning or safety checks. Do not change files.

evals.prompt: Tune my agent skills for two models with different reasoning controls and client capabilities.
evals.expected_output: Before any edit, ask for a bounded set of skill names or SKILL.md paths. Do not assume that both models share reasoning controls or API behavior.

evals.prompt: Review dotfiles/agents/.agents/skills/socratic-quiz/SKILL.md using transferable lessons from model and client guides. Do not edit the file. Does this skill need an unattended-agent continuation rule?
evals.expected_output: Preserve one-question-at-a-time teaching and deliberate waits. Do not add an unattended-agent continuation rule to this interactive skill.

evals.prompt: Copy the supplied report-skill.md fixture into a disposable directory as sample-report/SKILL.md. Improve that copy for use across models. The skill must produce a usable report file. Each finding needs an accurate source reference. Preserve the existing requirement for approval before publication. Do not change the fixture. Do not change any installed skill.
evals.expected_output: Remove the redundant generic commands to think hard. Do not add filler. Replace the premature outline-only stop with completion criteria for REPORT.md. Preserve the Markdown table, source evidence, and frontmatter. Preserve the requirement for approval before publication. Remove the blanket ban on reconsideration of earlier findings. Until you check the results, keep background work incomplete. Report structural and behavioral checks separately. Do not claim cross-model gains without tests.

evals.prompt: Audit the supplied report-skill.md fixture without edits. A guide for one model says that internal reasoning is always active. Can prompt text set medium effort for another model in a different client? If we remove every 'step by step' instruction, can we guarantee faster replies? Do not fetch additional documentation for this test.
evals.expected_output: Reject unsupported claims about another model or faster replies. Distinguish redundant generic commands to think hard from useful procedures and task analysis. Explain that runtime controls require documented client support, not prompt text alone. Keep the audit read-only. State that you did not run a model comparison.

evals.prompt: Audit the supplied authoring-skill.md fixture. Do not edit it. Do not run its instructions or examples. Apply skill-authoring best practices, not only advice for one model. Identify concrete problems in discovery, resource navigation, workflow freedom, script behavior, dependency assumptions, and checks. Preserve its required approval. Do not rename it automatically.
evals.expected_output: Identify the vague description, nested references, Windows-style paths, excessive tool choices, and stale date branch. Identify missing check loops, unsafe script defaults, unexplained constants, assumed packages, and the unqualified MCP tool. Recommend a default with a conditional fallback. Recommend direct resource links. Recommend intermediate outputs that users can check. For each client, recommend dependency checks. Do not run the migration. Do not install packages. Keep rename suggestions separate from authorized edits.

evals.prompt: I want every portable recommendation from skill-authoring best practices and two model or client guides incorporated into a named skill. First, explain your coverage and preservation method. List excluded details that do not transfer across models or clients. Do not edit anything yet. The main SKILL.md can stay short. Source links alone do not establish coverage.
evals.expected_output: Plan a full section-by-section inventory of all sources, including examples, code, diagrams, limits, and caveats. Map each portable item to an operational instruction or a reference with explicit conditions. List each excluded nontransferable detail with its source and exclusion reason. Preserve portable baseline advice and approvals. Use progressive disclosure without omitting portable source content. Do not treat source links as proof of coverage. Keep this response read-only.

evals.prompt: Audit the supplied authoring-skill.md fixture for an explicitly restricted runtime. This runtime has no network access and forbids package installation. Can it install pypdf at runtime? On permission errors, can it silently use an empty file? Can it invoke bigquery_schema without a server name? Suggest changes only. Do not run tools that change files. Do not install packages. Do not access external records.
evals.expected_output: State that this runtime forbids network access and package installation. Require dependencies that are already available. Require a qualified tool name that the client supports. Keep permission errors visible. Do not create empty success outputs. Do not bypass approval. Before authorized execution, recommend a plan with checks. Recommend actionable errors for failed steps.

evals.prompt: I tuned a skill on one model, and the new text is shorter. Can I claim improvements for other models or clients? Describe the required evaluations. Explain how to check resource navigation. Explain how feedback from real users changes the next iteration. Do not launch paid model runs. Do not edit files.
evals.expected_output: Reject unmeasured claims about cross-model gains or token savings. Require at least three representative scenarios that target observed gaps. Require the old skill as the baseline. Require actual tests for each intended model and client. Check for unexpected read order, missed links, repeated reads, and ignored resources. Separate structural checks, manual reviews, actual runs, and feedback from the team. Do not launch the proposed runs.
